incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered: INC-2028-047 — surge of fallback traffic to us-west-2 causing model-serving errors and elevated p50/p99 latency. Paging Maya S. (oncall).
Maya S.: I’m on it. seeing a big spike in 502/504s from the inference gateway.
Linus K.: looking at routing service logs — a recent policy change rolled out ~10m ago that widened allowed fallback variants to include v1.1 and v1.0 for cost-tier customers. could be oscillation.
Samir P.: linking infra metrics — us-west-2 GPU pool saturating, queue length climbing, OOMs on some pods.
Tess L.: service graph shows most traffic originated from cross-region reroutes from eu-west-1 -> us-west-2 after region fallback kicked in.
Nate R.: support tickets—2 customers reporting elevated latency, one complaining about 5xxs. tier-1 flagged it as P1.
Maya S.: hypothesis: client retry behavior + routing fallback is amplifying traffic into us-west-2 (retry storm). clients retry on 50x -> routing fails over to us-west-2 -> capacity overloaded -> more 50x -> clients retry again. feedback loop.
Elaine M.: Any recent change to smart-routing config? I asked for a small tweak earlier to prefer lower-cost regions.
Linus K.: yes, tuesday we loosened the fallback policy to allow more aggressive cross-region fallbacks for cost-savings — rollout went to 100% ~12:05UTC. matches timing.
Maya S.: ok immediate mitigations: 1) pause cross-region fallback policy 2) limit per-model fallback concurrency 3) push a temporary server-side 429 throttle for fallback attempts.
Samir P.: I can flip fallback policy to fail-closed. command to run: \n```\nrictl routing update-policy --name smart-fallback --set enabled=false --env production\n```\nSamir P.: executing now.
incident-bot: routing policy smart-fallback disabled by Samir P. at 1829123502.
Maya S.: great. next: reduce retry amplification by telling gateway to return Retry-After / 429 for overflow rather than 502. Linus, can you change fallback handler?
Linus K.: on it. changing behavior to short-circuit fallback when target model pool > 80% utilization. patch: \n```yaml\nfallback_policy:\n  max_fallbacks: 1\n  target_utilization_threshold: 0.8\n  on_over_threshold: return_429\n```\nLinus K.: deployed to canary. rolling to prod now.
SDK Bot: FYI — server returned Retry-After in 429 is surfaced to SDKs as Retry-After header, SDK teams should ensure backoff.
Maya S.: alerting thresholds updated to reduce noise. Also enable per-customer rate limiting for customers with repeated exchanges to the failing pools.
Tess L.: adding temporary circuit-breaker rule in route table to divert non-critical traffic to fallback-degraded (small model) pool: \n```\nrictl routes set-circuit-breaker --route /v1/generate --threshold 50 --action degrade\n```\nMaya S.: Nate, can you contact the two affected customers with an interim status that we're rolling mitigations and they may see reduced quality but improved availability?
Nate R.: on it. sending messages now.
Elaine M.: we should also assess SLA exposure for dedicated customers. Any impacted tenants?
Samir P.: one dedicated tenant saw a spike; support is already on a zoom with them. Samir P.: creating incident ticket INC-2028-047 in tracker and flagging legal/compliance per process.
Linus K.: after disabling fallback, I'm still seeing a short-lived surge due to client retries queued in the edge proxies — they'll drain over ~30s. adding an explicit backend drain command for overloaded pool.
Maya S.: run drain: \n```\nrictl pool drain --pool us-west-2-gpu-pool --grace-period 30\n```\nSamir P.: done. draining.
incident-bot: CPU/GPU metrics: us-west-2 GPU util 98% -> 62% after policy disable and drain within 3m. p99 latency reduced from 2.1s -> 450ms.
Maya S.: good. post-mortem notes so far: root cause chain = routing policy loosened (wider fallback variants) + no utilization gating on fallback + client retry behavior with tight retry windows -> amplification and failover storm.
Linus K.: follow-ups: 1) add utilization gating to routing logic 2) add per-route circuit-breaker 3) limit cross-region fallback rollout cadence 4) add server-side jitter header for SDKs 5) add telemetry to detect amplified failover loops.
SDK Bot: SDK update plan: make default client retry use exponential backoff with jitter (base 300ms, max 8s), surface server Retry-After header. we'll target patch release in next 48h.
Elaine M.: communications: prepare status page update and postmortem. message to sales for any enterprise customers potentially impacted.
Nate R.: support note posted. customers notified.
Maya S.: assigning owners: Linus (routing code changes + gating), Samir (policy rollout controls + infra knobs), Tess (circuit-breaker + route controls), SDK Bot / SDK team (client backoff), Elaine (comms + postmortem).
Linus K.: creating PRs now. blocking item — need to ensure we have a safe rollback for policy changes; propose requiring manual approval for any change that widens fallback set.
Samir P.: agreed. I'll add a rollout guard in the control plane for 7-day audits.
Maya S.: once metrics stable for 15m, we'll move to remediation -> postmortem. current status: mitigated, customer impact reduced, still monitoring.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2028-047 status updated to Mitigated at 1829123721.
Maya S.: leaving this thread to postmortem doc later. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Nate R.: closing support P1 after confirmation from customers.
Linus K.: quick note for oncall: in future, treat fallback widenings as high-risk for client-side retry interactions. add to runbook.
Maya S.: agreed — adding a new checklist item: verify fallback gating and retry behavior before rollout.
Elaine M.: will draft postmortem, ETA 24h.
Samir P.: exporting logs and linking to ticket. done.
incident-bot: thread closed for incident INC-2028-047 at 1829123840.
